annotationRationale: The main subject is determining reflection axes from corresponding points. The coordinate route uses perpendicular feet and midpoints; the alternative derives the rotation effect from reflection symmetry and elementary angle arithmetic, then uses a square. This explicit derivation needs no separate composition-theorem node. The midpoint node is used only at ratio 1:1 and has no supplied CN link. The supplied US rigid-motion and slope links provide partial overlap; perpendicular-slope criteria are applied rather than proved.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct. No area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently reflecting P gives P' = (32/13, 43/13). The midpoint of P'P'' is (42/13, 28/13), and that segment has slope -3/2. Its perpendicular bisector through the origin is therefore 2x - 3y = 0, choice D, distinct from the first mirror. No question, choice, or figure conflict occurs.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The coordinate midpoint route and the derived rotation plus square construction are genuinely different accessible methods. Together they cover the useful supplied approaches; no additional route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Reflection symmetry is appropriately assessed. Coordinate midpoints and general line equations are appropriate supports. The candidate methods do not rely on the existing mapping's vector route.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct. No area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The perpendicular line through P is correctly formed, giving H = (19/26, 95/26). Recovering the reflected endpoint gives P' = (32/13, 43/13), and the second midpoint is K = (42/13, 28/13). Since K is nonzero, the origin and K determine m uniquely with slope 2/3. All arithmetic and the final choice are correct.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Faithfully follows the valid coordinate route in AoPS Solution 3, using independently written explanations and explicit midpoint recovery. source-informed-original accurately identifies the third-party basis; no official MAA attribution is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The perpendicular-bisector property explains why the first construction works. The line intersection, reflected coordinates, and second midpoint are shown explicitly. The given origin condition then supplies the second point needed to determine m.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All five immediate IDs are used directly: reflection symmetry, perpendicular slopes, point-slope form, line intersection, and the midpoint case of segment partitioning.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The direction calculation gives a rotation through twice the directed mirror-angle difference. The observed clockwise quarter-turn therefore forces m to be 45 degrees clockwise from l, modulo a half-turn, determining one line. The square built from (1,5) and (5,-1) has center (3,2); its diagonal supplies the required direction and slope 2/3.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly combines the reflection-composition observation in LIVE and AoPS with AoPS Solution 2's square construction. The signed-angle derivation is supplied independently, and the LIVE trigonometric shortcut is not used. source-informed-original is appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation derives the reflection direction rule, handles full-turn and half-turn ambiguity explicitly, and explains why distance preservation makes the composition a rotation. The square construction then converts the angle information into coordinates without trigonometry. The words suffice without a diagram.

The composition result is derived from these concepts rather than invoked as an unexplained prerequisite.
